newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Big Australian wheat crop seen in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Big Australian wheat crop seen in 1997/98.

text.p: Australia is likely to produce anothe bigger than normal wheat crop in 1997/98 after its record 1996/97 crop, Australian Wheat Board officials said on Thursday.
The official forecasts would emerge at the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) Outlook '97 conference in the first week of February, they told Reuters.
It is unlikely the official forecaster will predict a new record for 1997/98, one year after the bumper crop just harvested, they said. But an above-average crop was expected.

Australia produces 15-16 million tonnes of wheat in a normal year, although in recent years production has dipped as low as 8.9 million tonnes in 1994/95 and 1982/83, and has risen as high as 22 million in 1983/84 and 23 million with the latest crop.
Australia's eastern-states wheat harvest has attracted most attention in the current harvest, now virtually complete.
As the harvest ends, New South Wales (NSW) has confirmed itself as the leading wheat producing state for the year with an officially-forecast crop of eight million tonnes of wheat.
But Western Australia (WA), which harvests slightly later than NSW, is also coming in strongly in the closing stages of its harvest with a record 7.7 million tonnes.

The AWB boosted WA's estimated latest wheat production to 7.7 million tonnes from the previous estimate of 7.2 million tonnes as part of its increased estimate for Australia as a whole of 23 million tonnes.
This was not announced as part of the AWB's increase in estimated Australia-wide production, but it put WA just behind NSW in 1996/97 production and onto a new state record.

NSW's expected eight million tonnes production of wheat in the current season compares with its record of 8.96 million tonnes in 1983/84, when Australia produced a record national crop of 22.0 million tonnes.
WA's current crop of 7.7 million, however, is far ahead of that state's previous record of 6.9 million tonnes in 1995/96.
WA's grain receivals have slowed in the past week or so to about 1,000 tonnes a day in a "bumper-to-bumper" harvest, state grain officials told Reuters on Thursday.

Queensland's harvest of a presently-estimated 2.1 million tonne wheat crop was virtually complete, with receivals so far of 2.3 million tonnes (including cross-border deliveries), grain officials said.
Victoria's 2.5 million tonne crop and South Australia's 2.7 million tonne crop were also just about all in, they said.
On Thursday, total grain receivals into the GrainCorp system in NSW stood at 8.19 million tonnes, up from 8.14 million tonnes a week ago, a spokesman said.
Receivals were running at about 5,000 tonnes a day, but the harvest was effectively complete, he said.
GrainCorp still believed that the previous record NSW grain receival, 8.3 million tonnes in 1983/84, would be surpassed by the current crop.
Officials believe that 400,000 tonnes to 500,000 tonnes of grain remain in warehouses and on-farm in the state.
